## 18 — Intersection S05 and S06

Viewed `readers/023/C/14_sigma05_06.png` once.

S05 has a visibly detached thin upper return whose right end folds back left, with a blank gap before the angular body. Its lower foot runs directly into the alpha loop. Its foot continues down into the long beta stem and loop. The raised sign has a horizontal cap and downward stem, with no separately recoverable upper arm. Retain B's complete Sigma_beta^+ | Sigma_beta^top alternatives and its literal B023-S06, with plus the qualified primary and the T-shaped alternative explicitly present. Do not add an upper arm. journal.literal:
## 28 — Complete formée, marked cup and S11

Viewed `readers/023/C/24_final_union_sigma.png` once.

Root sees the full formée word: tall f stem and left loop, low disconnected following letter runs, a separate raised acute-like mark, and a separate final e run. The f's descending stem meets the right stem of the lower cup at one continuous junction. Preserve that continuation once; neither a second printed f nor a duplicate cup-right stalk is supplied. The cup's upper left stalk is visibly interrupted into short segments above its horizontal cross-run. That high cross-run definitely exists and stops before the right stem, resolving original C023-R16's presence question. Its operation/attachment role remains qualified; H's disjoint-union note supplies no ink interpretation. Select C023-G17, including the complete word, interrupted left stalk, cross and full alpha-in-K limit. S11 has a separate roof, then a detached short head, then the angular body: preserve C023-G19 with its own head/independent-run question, definite roof, two-armed plus and continuous alpha. The final period is distinct and supplied once by the containing corollary group. Confidence high for physical junction/cross and local strokes; cross/head roles remain undetermined.

root_crop_evidence.observation: Root observed full formée with tall f/left loop, disconnected following runs, separate acute-like mark and final e. The descending f joins the cup's right stem continuously. The cup's upper-left stalk is interrupted; its definite high cross stops before the right stem. S11 has a separate roof, detached short head, angular body, two-armed plus and continuous alpha; its period is separate.

journal.literal:
## 29 — Interrupted left corollary rule

Viewed `readers/023/B/24_left_rule.png` once.

A draws two runs, C four, B six runs plus a bead. Root sees multiple pale interruptions down the upper and middle rule, a distinct small low bead between gaps, then a long darker lower run bending gradually right and ending in a thick terminal. Preserve B023-G10's six-run-plus-bead representation as the most complete of the supplied literal sequences. It is one physical marginal rule; the separate commands record its gaps rather than separate inventory elements. Copy those full-scan-coordinate path commands into the C023-G15 containing corollary frame, replacing C's four rule paths; keep C's parent units and all adjoining words once. The upper sloping heading underline is separate context. Confidence high for the rule and interruptions, medium for the manual segmentation approximation.

root_historical_journal.literal:
## 26 — Pi, full K and raised ring

Viewed `readers/023/C/22_pi.png` once.

Root sees the long Pi head, an attached left stem with a short low return, and a second right stem beginning below the head. The lower K has a long upright and an explicitly hooked lower-right arm. The raised mark is a small closed ring with a short left entry hook; its strokes alone leave circle versus zero unresolved. Preserve C023-G16's complete literal Pi/K/ring group, with complete candidates Pi_K^circ | Pi_K^0, retaining original C023-R13. The literal K avoids losing its low hook. Confidence high for the geometry, medium/qualified for ring identity.

## 27 — S10 retraced index, plus and two points

Viewed `readers/023/C/23_sigma10.png` once.

Root sees a joined Sigma head/body. The lower alpha-like loop is doubled/retraced, with a separate dark point above-left; the point can accompany a predecessor i or a separate trace, but stroke chronology is unresolved. Preserve the complete states Sigma_alpha^+ with both points | Sigma_(deleted i then alpha)^+ with the upper point retained. The raised plus has a vertical, main horizontal and an additional short upper-left cross-run; a second tiny point lies above-right. Both points are visible, against A's one-point source. Use C023-G18's complete literal geometry and add B's full predecessor-i/alpha state to its annotation; retain C's distinct local point/extra-run attachment qualifications. Each point occurs once, with hand/role/origin undetermined independently of the surrounding handwritten glyph. The following (alpha in K) is separate and unchanged. Confidence high for the parts, low for predecessor/cancellation chronology, medium for local attachment roles.

## 28 — Complete formée, marked cup and S11

Viewed `readers/023/C/24_final_union_sigma.png` once.

Root sees the full formée word: tall f stem and left loop, low disconnected following letter runs, a separate raised acute-like mark, and a separate final e run. The f's descending stem meets the right stem of the lower cup at one continuous junction. Preserve that continuation once; neither a second printed f nor a duplicate cup-right stalk is supplied. The cup's upper left stalk is visibly interrupted into short segments above its horizontal cross-run. That high cross-run definitely exists and stops before the right stem, resolving original C023-R16's presence question. Its operation/attachment role remains qualified; H's disjoint-union note supplies no ink interpretation. Select C023-G17, including the complete word, interrupted left stalk, cross and full alpha-in-K limit. S11 has a separate roof, then a detached short head, then the angular body: preserve C023-G19 with its own head/independent-run question, definite roof, two-armed plus and continuous alpha. The final period is distinct and supplied once by the containing corollary group. Confidence high for physical junction/cross and local strokes; cross/head roles remain undetermined.

## 29 — Interrupted left corollary rule

Viewed `readers/023/B/24_left_rule.png` once.

A draws two runs, C four, B six runs plus a bead. Root sees multiple pale interruptions down the upper and middle rule, a distinct small low bead between gaps, then a long darker lower run bending gradually right and ending in a thick terminal. Preserve B023-G10's six-run-plus-bead representation as the most complete of the supplied literal sequences. It is one physical marginal rule; the separate commands record its gaps rather than separate inventory elements. Copy those full-scan-coordinate path commands into the C023-G15 containing corollary frame, replacing C's four rule paths; keep C's parent units and all adjoining words once. The upper sloping heading underline is separate context. Confidence high for the rule and interruptions, medium for the manual segmentation approximation.

## 28 — Complete formée, marked cup and S11

Viewed `readers/023/C/24_final_union_sigma.png` once.

Root sees the full formée word: tall f stem and left loop, low disconnected following letter runs, a separate raised acute-like mark, and a separate final e run. The cup's upper left stalk is visibly interrupted into short segments above its horizontal cross-run. That high cross-run definitely exists and stops before the right stem, resolving original C023-R16's presence question. Its operation/attachment role remains qualified; H's disjoint-union note supplies no ink interpretation. Select C023-G17, including the complete word, interrupted left stalk, cross and full alpha-in-K limit. S11 has a separate roof, then a detached short head, then the angular body: preserve C023-G19 with its own head/independent-run question, definite roof, two-armed plus and continuous alpha. The final period is distinct and supplied once by the containing corollary group. Confidence high for physical junction/cross and local strokes; cross/head roles remain undetermined.

## 28 — Complete formée, marked cup and S11

Viewed `readers/023/C/24_final_union_sigma.png` once.

Root sees the full formée word: tall f stem and left loop, low disconnected following letter runs, a separate raised acute-like mark, and a separate final e run. The f's descending stem meets the right stem of the lower cup at one continuous junction. Preserve that continuation once; neither a second printed f nor a duplicate cup-right stalk is supplied. ## 01 — Opening prouvons

Viewed `readers/023/C/02_prouvons.png` once.

A and C print prouvons firm; B prints unsure{prouvons}; both witnesses print the word without qualification. Root sees a long looped descending p, a short upturned following run, several disconnected short horizontal/oblique runs, and a low final right hook. The interior letter bodies are heavily reduced. Preserve the complete primary word as \unsure{prouvons}, with no invented alternative. The following que l'on is distinct and remains live. This is a new local qualification, not a resolution of an original C doubt row. Confidence medium.

## 02 — Opening a-shaped point

Viewed `readers/023/C/01_opening_a.png` once.

A and B retain a versus an independent/point-shaped mark; C prints a firm. Both witnesses supply a. Root sees a small solid horizontal lozenge, tapering at the left with a thicker upper-right corner; no open counter or separate stem is recoverable. Preserve this exact visible shape once, with complete candidates a | point-shaped independent mark and unresolved role/hand/origin, using B023-G01 as the literal donor. The following barred V, intersection, E_beta, equals and empty-set are clear. Do not replace the shape by a firm ordinary a. Confidence medium for the primary, high for the mark's presence.

## 03 — Cancelled contient and raised rencontre

Viewed `readers/023/A/02_replacement.png` once.

All three readers put deleted contient below raised inserted rencontre; H leaves rencontre unmarked as an insertion. Root sees the lower c-on-t-i-ent sequence crossed by one long near-horizontal rule, with an ascender and dot surviving above it. The raised rencontre has its own upper baseline and no cancellation crossing it. The separate following aucun is live. Preserve \deleted{contient} \inserted{rencontre} aucun, with the complete insertion scope. Confidence high for the deletion and raised placement. The preceding ne is outside this crop and its exact order will receive a separate local view rather than being claimed from this image.

## 04 — Detached left trace beside first inclusion

Viewed `readers/023/A/17_left_mark.png` once.

A and C preserve this trace; B and both witnesses omit it. Root sees a small dark triangular point with a fading short lower tail in the blank left margin, separated by a broad blank interval from E_beta. Preserve it once as the literal C023-G01 donor, locally qualified for role, hand and surface origin. No punctuation or mathematical operation is assigned. Its presence is high-confidence; attribution remains undetermined.

## 05 — First union and corrected hatted Sigma

Viewed `readers/023/C/03_first_union_sigma.png` once.

Original C023-R14 and C023-R01 remain unresolved in their full original scopes. Root sees a rounded outer cup with tall right stalk and a second oblique descending through the left stalk to an upturned inner end. Preserve complete states deleted(bigvee) followed by bigcup_(alpha in K) | retraced live bigcup_(alpha in K); H's plain union alone omits this inner run. Use C023-G02, including its complete limit once. In the next glyph a separate roof is clear, the Sigma head joins the angular body, and a thick additional upright crosses its interior and foot. The upright supplies no recoverable separate middle horizontal for an E and no secure chronology. Preserve all three complete states widehat{deleted I Sigma}_alpha^+ | widehat{deleted E Sigma}_alpha^+ | widehat{Sigma}_alpha^+ with internal retrace, primary I, using C023-G03. Roof, both arms of plus and lower alpha are definite. Both historical rows retained; the local geometry is high-confidence and predecessor identity/state low-confidence.

## 06 — Cancelled donc si and its endpoint

Viewed `readers/023/C/04_donc_si.png` once.

All three readers retain the cancelled doubtful donc si; H additionally supplies an unreadable item. Root sees a looped d ascender, low interrupted remnants before a distinct short s-like rise and detached i dot, all crossed by one continuous rule. The rule then runs through blank space and ends before the separate descending j of je. No third word-body is recoverable there. Preserve \deleted{\unsure{donc si}}; retain original C023-R02 as unresolved over the whole two-word cancelled scope. H023-ILL01 is recorded as the extra placeholder whose corresponding separate word is not supported by this crop. Confidence medium for the two-word reading, high for the cancellation and the blank endpoint interval.

## 07 — Reduced on a and ochre trace

Viewed `readers/023/C/05_on_a.png` once.

A qualifies the whole on a; B keeps on firm and retains a/point locally through its first occurrence; C prints on a firm. Root sees the first short hook and second low arch separated by blank gaps, then a compact filled c/lozenge-like a with no distinct counter. Retain a local qualification over the complete on a phrase, primary on a; the point-shaped-mark alternative concerns its final a alone. Preserve the a's literal small shape, taking B023-G04's a component while extending the group to own the preceding on once; en fait remains outside. The detached ochre oblique above-right is clearly separate from both words and has a short down-right slant; retain it once with role, hand and surface origin undetermined. B's trace or C023-G04-P01 may be used with its exact local position, never duplicated. Confidence medium for the phrase, high for the separate trace's presence.

## 08 — Displayed E foot and S02

Viewed `readers/023/B/07_display_sigma.png` once.

Only B reproduces the displayed E's extra lower return. Root sees a distinct low closed horizontal loop/retrace along E's foot; preserve the entire E_beta once using B023-G05, including its curved body, middle bar, lower loop and beta. No predecessor letter or cancellation state is inferred. The unroofed S02 has a head meeting its upper-left diagonal, one angular body, a clear lower alpha and a two-armed raised plus. It may remain ordinary Sigma_alpha^+; no detached-run qualifier belongs to this local S02. The displayed cup has a rounded base and no extra inner diagonal. Confidence high.

## 09 — Complete slanted marginal note

Viewed `readers/023/C/06_margin.png` once.

The whole three-line note is visible upright after the supplied rotation. Root reads C'est trivial, followed by one compact cancelled item, then du fait que les E_i (i in I/J), then sont disjoints. The initial C has a tall open curved bowl, supporting the capital against H's lowercase. The compact item has a black crossing over joined loops and a short right descender; its letters cannot be recovered, so preserve \deleted{\illegible{1}} and retain original C023-R03. The parenthetical letter has an upper cap, descending stem and left-returning lower foot; the lower turn does not securely distinguish I from J. Retain original C023-R04 as I|J, despite B's firm I. Preserve all three lines, their original order and complete closing parenthesis. C and A's full marginal source is suitable. Main-line ce/qui seen in adjoining context is reserved for its separately planned unrotated target; no main-line attachment is decided here. Capital and deletion placement high-confidence; I/J low-confidence.

## 10 — ce qui, prouvera and assertion point

Viewed `readers/023/B/09_ce_qui_prouvera.png` once.

A offers qui|ce qui, B ce-or-empty before qui, C firm ce qui; H has qui. Root sees a low curved ce-like run immediately left of the clear q-descender/u/i sequence, close to and partly crowded by the slanted note. Its attachment remains uncertain. Preserve complete candidates \unsure{ce qui|qui}, primary ce qui, rather than an empty word alternative. The verb has a clear descending looped p, reduced low intermediate strokes, and an additional shallow final arch/point before l'assertion. The ending is insufficiently articulated to settle prouvera against prouve: preserve \unsure{prouvera|prouve}, retaining original C023-R05. A and C's separate lower-right point beneath l'assertion is visibly present, far below the word baseline; B omits it. Preserve C023-G05's word and point once, with the point's role, hand and surface origin undetermined. Confidence medium for the verbal readings, high for point presence.

## 11 — Cela revient au

Viewed `readers/023/B/10_cela_revient_au.png` once.

All readers read revient against H's résulte. Root sees the low r entrance, successive pointed/minim curves, a detached i dot and a terminal t-like crossed rise; read revient. The following short group is almost a single shallow rising run with a right downturn, leaving its two letters reduced. Preserve Cela revient \unsure{au}; retain original C023-R06 rather than adopting B's firm au. The crop shows no tall initial ascender for H's du. Confidence high for revient, medium for au.

## 12 — Position of live ne before the correction

Viewed `crops/scan023_ne_order.png` once.

This new crop addresses only the still-unseen placement target following En effet. Root sees V followed on the same baseline by the short live ne, with no crossing rule over either. This line precedes the cancelled contient and raised rencontre already inspected in section 03. Preserve V ne \deleted{contient} \inserted{rencontre}; H's placement of cancelled contient before ne is not the page order. The neighboring effet ascenders and following E_i context extend beyond the crop, while V ne is complete. Confidence high. No target from section 03 was reopened.

## 13 — S04 upper run and pale connection

Viewed `readers/023/C/11_sigma04.png` once.

A and B encode S04 as an ordinary joined Sigma; C preserves a short upper run, lower body and faint bridge candidate. Root sees a heavy upper bar with short downward spurs near its left end and the body's diagonal beginning below and slightly right of that end. A pale narrow connection is possible between them, but its continuity cannot be secured. Preserve C023-G06's complete literal group, including its faint bridge, plus and alpha, with local complete candidates Sigma with a pale head/body bridge | angular body accompanied by a separate short upper run. This is the first printed recurring head-role qualifier on this page. No roof is supplied. Plus and alpha are definite; the head connection/role remains qualified. Confidence medium.

## 14 — Lemma tels and cancelled tel que les

Viewed `readers/023/C/12_tels.png` once.

A and C retain a tels qualification; B resolves it. Root sees the live word's tall t stem with low crossing/loop, a distinct following e/l loop sequence, and the short descending terminal s before the separate que. Read tels firm and resolve original C023-R07. The upper tel que les is crossed throughout by one long rising rule, with the q descender below and the final l ascender above; preserve its complete deleted scope. The small preceding entry stroke belongs to the approach to tels and does not support an additional word. Confidence medium-high for tels, high for the cancelled three-word scope.

## 15 — Cancelled et before des

Viewed `crops/scan023_deleted_et.png` once.

All three readers and C mark et deleted; H gives it live. Root sees the low loop and tall t crossed by a straight heavy horizontal extending left across the whole short word and beyond its right edge. The following des is separated by blank paper and has no such crossing. Preserve \deleted{et} des. The upper heading underline is separately visible and does not account for the local crossing. Confidence high for the local cancellation.

## 16 — Isolated point beside lemma

Viewed `readers/023/B/25_left_small_point.png` once.

B alone supplies this isolated point. Root sees one small solid near-round black point, surrounded by blank paper with no attached letter or line. Preserve B023-M02 once with role, hand, attachment and surface origin undetermined. Its physical presence is high-confidence; no manuscript punctuation or mathematical operation is inferred.

## 17 — First relation and repeated inequality

Viewed `readers/023/C/13_first_relation.png` once.

Root sees two short horizontal bars crossed by a much heavier curved descending stroke that ends in a leftward low hook. The extra weight and hook permit both reported complete states: alpha ne beta in K | alpha deleted(ne), beta in K. Their chronology/target is not settled by the overlaps. Retain original C023-R15 and preserve C023-G07's full relation geometry and lower hook once. The later comma after K and repeated alpha ne beta are visibly separate and remain as written; no mathematical redundancy is removed. Confidence high for the two bars/hook, low for the alternative deletion/comma interpretation.

Viewed `readers/023/C/14_sigma05_06.png` once.

S05 has a visibly detached thin upper return whose right end folds back left, with a blank gap before the angular body. Its lower foot runs directly into the alpha loop. Preserve C023-G08's complete head/body/shared-alpha/plus, retaining the local head-versus-independent-upper-run qualification already first printed at S04. S06 differs: its narrow folded upper return comes back to the left entry of the body through a faint continuous bend; root selects the joined-head geometry recorded by B/C, against A's detached/pale-break role. Its foot continues down into the long beta stem and loop. The raised sign has a horizontal cap and downward stem, with no separately recoverable upper arm. Retain B's complete Sigma_beta^+ | Sigma_beta^top alternatives and its literal B023-S06, with plus the qualified primary and the T-shaped alternative explicitly present. Do not add an upper arm. Intersection, equals, empty-set and full stop are separate and retained. Head/body and shared-index geometry high-confidence; raised-sign identity medium/qualified.

## 19 — S07 detached head and alpha terminal point

Viewed `readers/023/C/15_sigma07.png` once.

Root sees a short horizontal upper run separated from the angular Sigma body by a definite white gap. Its local head/independent-run role remains qualified, with no roof supplied. The raised plus has both horizontal and vertical arms. The lower alpha loop has a rising terminal whose dark upper point is separated from the heavier lower stroke by a very pale neck. A/B render alpha ordinarily; C preserves this local point and its attachment doubt. Preserve C023-G10 in full: alpha with separated terminal point | alpha accompanied by an independent point. Keep the small point's role/hand/origin undetermined and the surrounding glyph in his hand; do not let the parent glyph's attribution erase this local qualification. The comma after the expression remains separate. Confidence high for visible parts, medium for terminal attachment.

Viewed `readers/023/C/16_conclusion_correction.png` once.

The same rising rule reaches the lower strokes of the raised que: it crosses the q descender and low u-like return below their upper bodies. Preserve C023-G11's full word-bearing group and single two-segment rule; do not add a second cancellation or duplicate an inserted word. Confidence high for placement and K gap, medium for participle and que target.

## 21 — S08 final lemma glyph

Viewed `readers/023/C/17_sigma08.png` once.

Root sees a separate short upper bar above the angular S08 body, with a clear blank left gap; preserve that local head/independent-run qualification and C023-G12's complete group. Its raised plus has a small upper arm above the crossbar, a long lower arm and two horizontal arms. The lower alpha is a continuous loop/rising-stroke form with no detached dot. The final full stop is separate to the right and remains present once. Confidence high for geometry and plus/alpha; upper-run role remains qualified at the established first occurrence.

## 22 — Unfinished live wording and right-hand points

Viewed `readers/023/C/18_provient_du.png` once.

Original C023-R09 retains its complete compound scope. Root sees a long looped p, tightly crossing following letter strokes, a detached short upright near the middle/end, and a stretched low terminal run ending in a loop. No secure acute over the first e is distinguishable. Preserve primary precise, with full alternatives précise, provient, precise le, précise le; do not split off le or infer an omitted completion. This keeps A/B's primary order while retaining C's accented reading and both two-word states. The following group has a d-like bowl/ascending stem, then one low u-shaped valley and an extended exit; root reads du and resolves original C023-R10 against des/sens. Preserve the two far-right points: the upper point is right of the lower point, with a clear blank gap between and from the wording. Use C023-G13 with du firm and its two local mark paths unchanged; mark role, hand and origin remain undetermined. H023-UNC01 applies to the verb and H023-ILL02 to the following short group; retain those distinct source marker locations. Confidence low for the full verb/word-boundary candidates, medium-high for du, high for both points.

## 23 — Pale oblique before Corollaire

Viewed `readers/023/B/26_left_small_slash.png` once.

B alone preserves the pale oblique left of Corollaire. Root sees a small grey oblong slanting up-right, well separated from the neighboring capital's main stroke. Preserve B023-M04 once with role, hand, attachment and surface origin undetermined. The neighboring capital is context and is partly clipped; the complete mark and its surrounding blank space are visible. Presence high-confidence; interpretation unresolved.

## 24 — Abbreviated préc.

Viewed `readers/023/C/19_prec.png` once.

A retains a qualification; B and C resolve préc. Root sees a long descending p, short following r/é body, a separate acute-like raised stroke above the low group, a short terminal c run, and a distinct abbreviation point before sur. Read préc. without expansion and resolve original C023-R11. H's précédentes supplies letters beyond this visible abbreviated form. The preceding hyp. remains abbreviated as all readers saw. Confidence high for abbreviation, medium-high for the local letters/accent.

## 25 — Complete corollary family and crowded index

Viewed `readers/023/C/20_family.png` once.

Root sees a separate S09 head above its body; the lower foot curves into a short right hook, with one detached point above that hook and a clear raised alpha. Preserve the hook/dot once, primary i, while retaining C's local i-attachment versus foot-retrace/independent-point role question and undetermined hand for the point. The closing parenthesis continues into the external alpha loop. The final index cluster has a left upright, two K-like obliques, an additional right loop and a thick right descending upright. A's firm K loses this overlapping state question. Retain original C023-R12 with all four complete family states: (Sigma_i^alpha)_(alpha in K), (Sigma_i^alpha)_(alpha in I), (Sigma_i^alpha)_(alpha in deleted(I)K), (Sigma_i^alpha)_(alpha in deleted(K)I), primary K, without assigning stroke chronology. Use the whole B023-G08 literal geometry because its extra right loop/upright is explicitly preserved; extend its candidate annotation to include the fourth state and the independent local dot-role qualification. The group owns both parentheses, external alpha/in/index and the final comma once. Confidence high for physical components, low for the overlapping index state.

## 26 — Pi, full K and raised ring

Viewed `readers/023/C/22_pi.png` once.

Root sees the long Pi head, an attached left stem with a short low return, and a second right stem beginning below the head. The lower K has a long upright and an explicitly hooked lower-right arm. The raised mark is a small closed ring with a short left entry hook; its strokes alone leave circle versus zero unresolved. Preserve C023-G16's complete literal Pi/K/ring group, with complete candidates Pi_K^circ | Pi_K^0, retaining original C023-R13. The literal K avoids losing its low hook. Confidence high for the geometry, medium/qualified for ring identity.

## 27 — S10 retraced index, plus and two points

Viewed `readers/023/C/23_sigma10.png` once.

Root sees a joined Sigma head/body. The lower alpha-like loop is doubled/retraced, with a separate dark point above-left; the point can accompany a predecessor i or a separate trace, but stroke chronology is unresolved. Preserve the complete states Sigma_alpha^+ with both points | Sigma_(deleted i then alpha)^+ with the upper point retained. The raised plus has a vertical, main horizontal and an additional short upper-left cross-run; a second tiny point lies above-right. Both points are visible, against A's one-point source. Use C023-G18's complete literal geometry and add B's full predecessor-i/alpha state to its annotation; retain C's distinct local point/extra-run attachment qualifications. Each point occurs once, with hand/role/origin undetermined independently of the surrounding handwritten glyph. The following (alpha in K) is separate and unchanged. Confidence high for the parts, low for predecessor/cancellation chronology, medium for local attachment roles.

## 28 — Complete formée, marked cup and S11

Viewed `readers/023/C/24_final_union_sigma.png` once.

Root sees the full formée word: tall f stem and left loop, low disconnected following letter runs, a separate raised acute-like mark, and a separate final e run. The f's descending stem meets the right stem of the lower cup at one continuous junction. Preserve that continuation once; neither a second printed f nor a duplicate cup-right stalk is supplied. The cup's upper left stalk is visibly interrupted into short segments above its horizontal cross-run. That high cross-run definitely exists and stops before the right stem, resolving original C023-R16's presence question. Its operation/attachment role remains qualified; H's disjoint-union note supplies no ink interpretation. Select C023-G17, including the complete word, interrupted left stalk, cross and full alpha-in-K limit. S11 has a separate roof, then a detached short head, then the angular body: preserve C023-G19 with its own head/independent-run question, definite roof, two-armed plus and continuous alpha. The final period is distinct and supplied once by the containing corollary group. Confidence high for physical junction/cross and local strokes; cross/head roles remain undetermined.

## 29 — Interrupted left corollary rule

Viewed `readers/023/B/24_left_rule.png` once.

A draws two runs, C four, B six runs plus a bead. Root sees multiple pale interruptions down the upper and middle rule, a distinct small low bead between gaps, then a long darker lower run bending gradually right and ending in a thick terminal. Preserve B023-G10's six-run-plus-bead representation as the most complete of the supplied literal sequences. It is one physical marginal rule; the separate commands record its gaps rather than separate inventory elements. Copy those full-scan-coordinate path commands into the C023-G15 containing corollary frame, replacing C's four rule paths; keep C's parent units and all adjoining words once. The upper sloping heading underline is separate context. Confidence high for the rule and interruptions, medium for the manual segmentation approximation.

## 30 — Final word accents and faint capital-side hook

Viewed `readers/023/C/25_final_accents.png` once.

B prints both final words firm; A and C preserve complete accent alternatives. Root sees the reduced Immédiat lettering with a tiny raised near-upright/point-like stroke over the e position, and a short raised bent point near the first e position of récurrence. Their direction/attachment is insufficient for an unqualified acute or grave. Preserve complete word candidates Immédiat|Immèdiat|Immediat and récurrence|rècurrence|recurrence, each scoped to its own whole word. A faint short curved hook is visible to the left of the capital's main stroke; only C supplies it. Preserve C023-G20's complete word-bearing group and that hook once, with hook role/hand/origin undetermined. par remains outside the group. This crop settles only these words and hook; the count/comparison at the end still requires its own target view. Confidence medium for word bodies and low for accent direction/attachment.

## 31 — Final card K comparison and endpoint

Viewed `readers/023/A/16_final_line.png` once.

This view addresses only the final count/comparison not present in section 30's target. Root sees sur card K at the end of the first line and, on the continuation, a greater-than angle with a separate lower rising stroke, then 0 and a full stop. Select A's \operatorname{card} K\geqslant 0, preserving the slant visible in the lower relation stroke, against B/C's \geq source spelling. The exact word accents and capital-side hook were already decided in section 30 and were not reconsidered from this wider context. The comparison is transcribed as the manuscript's statement, with no proof check. Confidence high.
